lessons.title: Verb Tenses Overview
lessons.description: Tell present from past from future without thinking — pick the right verb form by spotting time signals.
lessons.rule: Each tense pairs with signal words. Spot the signal, pick the form.

tldr.rule: Signal word → tense. 'Yesterday' = past, 'since' = present perfect, 'tomorrow' = future.
tldr.example: I saw her yesterday. I have known her since 2020.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Tôi gặp cô ấy hôm qua. Tôi biết cô ấy từ năm 2020.

scenarios.why: Past actions with a clear when → simple past.
scenarios.english: I had pho for lunch yesterday.
scenarios.vietnamese: Hôm qua tôi ăn phở trưa.

scenarios.context: 💼 Saying how long you've worked somewhere
scenarios.why: Started in past, still true now → present perfect with 'for'/'since'.
scenarios.english: I've worked at this company for three years.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi đã làm ở công ty này được ba năm.

scenarios.why: Future arrangement → 'will' for decisions, 'going to' for plans.
scenarios.english: I'll text you when I arrive.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi sẽ nhắn khi đến nơi.

scenarios.why: Habits/repeated actions → simple present.
scenarios.english: She drinks coffee every morning.
scenarios.vietnamese: Cô ấy uống cà phê mỗi sáng.

quickChecks.question: She ___ to Hanoi last summer.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Last summer' is a finished past time → simple past 'went'.

quickChecks.question: I ___ him since 2019.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Since' signals a state that started in the past and continues → present perfect.

quickChecks.question: Tomorrow we ___ to the new cafe.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Tomorrow' → future. After 'will', use the base form ('go'), not '-ing'.

quickChecks.question: Water ___ at 100°C.
quickChecks.explanation: Universal facts → simple present. Subject 'water' (singular) → 'boils'.

sections.heading: Simple Present — habits & facts
sections.body: For routines, repeated actions, and universal truths.
bullets: Signals: every day, usually, always, often, sometimes
3rd person singular (he/she/it) takes -s/-es

examples.english: She drinks coffee every morning.
examples.vietnamese: Cô ấy uống cà phê mỗi sáng.

examples.english: Water boils at 100°C.

sections.heading: Simple Past — finished, dated
sections.body: Action completed at a specific time in the past.
bullets: Signals: yesterday, last week, ago, in 2020
Negative uses 'didn't + base verb' (NOT past form)

examples.english: I visited Hue last summer.
examples.vietnamese: Tôi đã đi Huế mùa hè năm ngoái.

examples.english: We didn't see the movie.
examples.note: Negative: didn't + see, NOT didn't + saw.

sections.heading: Present Perfect — past affecting now
sections.body: Bridges past and present: experience up to now, or actions that started before and continue.
bullets: Signals: since, for, already, yet, just, ever, never
have/has + V3 (past participle)

examples.english: I have lived in Hanoi for 5 years.
examples.vietnamese: Tôi đã sống ở Hà Nội 5 năm (vẫn còn).

sections.heading: Simple Future — predictions, decisions
sections.body: For things that haven't happened yet.
bullets: Signals: tomorrow, next week, soon
will + base verb (no 'to', no -ing)

examples.english: It will rain tonight.
examples.vietnamese: Tối nay trời sẽ mưa.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt không chia động từ → nhớ thêm -s ở 'he/she/it' và đổi V → V2 cho quá khứ.
'Yesterday', 'last…', 'ago' luôn đi với simple past, KHÔNG đi với present perfect.
Sau 'will' luôn là động từ nguyên thể, không bao giờ V2 hay -ing.

commonMistakes.explanation: 'Yesterday' = thời điểm xác định → simple past.
Sau 'will' luôn dùng V nguyên thể.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi đã ăn tối với gia đình tuần trước.
practice.english: I had dinner with my family last week.

practice.vietnamese: Cô ấy đã sống ở đây từ năm 2020.
practice.english: She has lived here since 2020.

practice.vietnamese: Ngày mai tôi sẽ học tiếng Anh.
practice.english: I will study English tomorrow.

lessons.title: Articles: a, an, the
lessons.description: Master a / an / the in 5 minutes — the #1 mistake for Vietnamese learners.
lessons.rule: 'a/an' = unknown one. 'the' = the specific one we both know. No article for general plurals.
examples: I bought a book. The book is great.

tldr.rule: First mention → a/an. Second mention or unique thing → the. General plural → nothing.
tldr.example: I saw a cat. The cat was orange. I love cats.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Tôi thấy một con mèo. Con mèo đó màu cam. Tôi thích mèo.

scenarios.why: Naming your job/role = singular countable → needs 'a/an'.
scenarios.english: I'm a software engineer.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi là kỹ sư phần mềm.

scenarios.why: Something general from the menu → 'a/an' for one item.
scenarios.english: I'll have a coffee and the chicken sandwich.
scenarios.vietnamese: Cho tôi một cà phê và món bánh mì gà.

scenarios.why: Most country names take no article. The Netherlands / The UK are exceptions.
scenarios.english: I live in Vietnam, but I've visited the UK.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi sống ở Việt Nam, nhưng đã đi Anh.

scenarios.why: Plural noun used in general sense → no article.
scenarios.english: I love reading books.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi thích đọc sách.

quickChecks.question: She is ___ honest person.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Honest' starts with a vowel SOUND (h is silent) → 'an'.

quickChecks.question: I love ___ music.
quickChecks.explanation: General love for music in general → no article. 'The music' = a specific song/genre.

quickChecks.question: We saw ___ amazing show. ___ show was incredible.
quickChecks.explanation: First time → 'an' (vowel sound). Second mention → 'the' (now specific).

quickChecks.question: He is ___ university student.
quickChecks.explanation: 'University' starts with /ju:/ — a consonant sound — so use 'a', not 'an'.

sections.heading: a vs an — by SOUND, not letter
sections.body: Use 'an' before a vowel sound; 'a' before a consonant sound. The rule is about pronunciation.

examples.english: an hour
examples.vietnamese: một giờ

examples.english: a university

sections.heading: When to use 'the'
sections.body: When the thing is specific or already known to both speakers.
bullets: Already mentioned (I saw a dog. The dog was…)
Unique (the sun, the moon, the Earth)
Superlatives & ordinals (the best, the first)

sections.heading: No article — general plurals & uncountables
sections.body: When talking about something in general, drop the article.

examples.english: Coffee is bitter.
Dogs are loyal animals.
I live in Vietnam.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt không có mạo từ → người Việt hay quên 'a/an/the'. Phản xạ: danh từ đếm được số ít LUÔN cần mạo từ.
Lần đầu nhắc → a/an. Nhắc lại → the. Quy tắc nhanh.

commonMistakes.explanation: 'Honest' bắt đầu bằng âm nguyên âm.

practice.vietnamese: Cô ấy là một giáo viên.
practice.english: She is a teacher.

practice.vietnamese: Mặt trời mọc ở hướng đông.
practice.english: The sun rises in the east.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi thích đọc sách.
practice.english: I like reading books.

lessons.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
lessons.description: Singular subject = singular verb. Sounds easy, but 'everyone', 'a lot of', 'there is/are' all hide traps.
lessons.rule: Match the verb to the subject. Singular → adds -s. Plural → no -s.

tldr.rule: He / she / it / singular noun → verb + s. 'Everyone' counts as singular.
tldr.example: Everyone is here. The team plays well.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Mọi người đều ở đây. Đội bóng chơi tốt.

scenarios.why: Collective nouns (team, family, staff) are usually singular in American English.
scenarios.english: The team is winning.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đội đang thắng.

scenarios.context: 🙋 Describing what people in your office do
scenarios.why: Plural subject → plural verb (no -s).
scenarios.english: My colleagues work remotely.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đồng nghiệp tôi làm việc từ xa.

scenarios.why: 'Everyone' looks plural but is grammatically singular.
scenarios.english: Everyone loves Friday.
scenarios.vietnamese: Ai cũng yêu thứ Sáu.

scenarios.context: 📋 Saying how many things there are
scenarios.why: 'There is' for 1; 'There are' for 2+ or 'a lot of [plural]'.
scenarios.english: There are five people in the meeting.
scenarios.vietnamese: Có 5 người trong cuộc họp.

quickChecks.question: She ___ to the gym every day.
quickChecks.explanation: Subject 'she' (3rd person singular) → verb + es.

quickChecks.question: Everyone in the room ___ excited.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular even though it feels plural.

quickChecks.question: There ___ many cars on the road today.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Cars' is plural → 'there are'.

quickChecks.question: My family ___ from Hue.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Family' is a collective noun, treated as singular here.

sections.heading: Basic rule — add -s at 3rd person singular
sections.body: In simple present, he/she/it + verb takes -s/-es.
bullets: I / you / we / they → base verb
he / she / it / singular noun → verb + s/es
Verbs ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o: add -es (watches, goes)

sections.heading: Indefinite pronouns — always singular
sections.body: Words that feel plural but grammatically count as one: everyone, somebody, each, neither, either.

examples.english: Everyone is here.
Neither answer is correct.

sections.heading: 'There is' vs 'There are'
sections.body: Match the verb to the noun right after it.

examples.english: There is a book on the table.
There are many books on the table.
There is some water in the bottle.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt không chia động từ. Phản xạ: thấy 'he/she/it' → thêm -s.
'Everyone/everybody' luôn đi với động từ số ít — đừng dịch theo nghĩa.

commonMistakes.wrong: He go to work by bus.
commonMistakes.right: He goes to work by bus.

practice.vietnamese: Cô ấy thường thức dậy lúc 6 giờ.
practice.english: She usually wakes up at 6.

practice.vietnamese: Có rất nhiều ô tô trên đường.
practice.english: There are many cars on the street.

practice.vietnamese: Mỗi học sinh đều có một quyển sách.
practice.english: Each student has a book.

lessons.title: Prepositions: in / on / at
lessons.description: Time and place prepositions follow a 'big to small' logic. Master 3 prepositions, cover 80% of cases.
lessons.rule: Big container → IN. Surface or date → ON. Specific point → AT.
examples: on Monday / on the table / on May 14
at 5 PM / at home / at the door

tldr.rule: Time/place from big to small: IN (year/month/country) → ON (day/surface) → AT (clock time/exact point).
tldr.example: I'll meet you at 5 PM on Friday in May.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Tôi sẽ gặp bạn lúc 5 giờ chiều thứ Sáu vào tháng Năm.

scenarios.why: Pick by precision: clock time → at, day → on, larger period → in.
scenarios.english: Class starts at 9 on Monday in September.
scenarios.vietnamese: Lớp bắt đầu lúc 9 giờ thứ Hai vào tháng Chín.

scenarios.why: Inside a place → in. At a point → at. On a surface → on.
scenarios.english: I'm at the cafe in District 1, sitting on the terrace.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi đang ở quán cà phê trong quận 1, ngồi trên ban công.

scenarios.why: Big vehicles → on. Small/private → in.
scenarios.english: I'm on the bus, but my friend is in a taxi.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi đang trên xe buýt, còn bạn tôi trong taxi.

scenarios.why: Specific date → on. Month only → in.
scenarios.english: My birthday is on May 14 — in May, basically.
scenarios.vietnamese: Sinh nhật tôi vào 14 tháng Năm — đại loại là tháng Năm.

quickChecks.question: I was born ___ May 14.
quickChecks.explanation: Specific date → 'on'.

quickChecks.question: I'll see you ___ 5 PM.
quickChecks.explanation: Exact clock time → 'at'.

quickChecks.question: She is ___ the kitchen.
quickChecks.explanation: Inside a space → 'in'.

quickChecks.question: I commute ___ the bus.
quickChecks.explanation: Public transport (bus, train, plane) → 'on'. Cars/taxis → 'in'.

sections.heading: Time — big to small
sections.body: Move from large period to single point: IN year/month → ON day → AT clock time.
bullets: IN: century, decade, year, month, season, parts of day (in the morning)
ON: specific day, date, holiday
AT: clock time, night, weekend

sections.heading: Place — same big-to-small logic
sections.body: IN inside a space, ON a surface, AT a precise point.

examples.english: She is in the kitchen.
The book is on the shelf.
I'll meet you at the cafe.

sections.heading: Exceptions to memorize
sections.body: A few cases break the pattern. Learn them as set phrases.
bullets: at night, in the morning/afternoon/evening
on time = punctual, in time = early enough
at home / at school / at work

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt dùng 'ở/vào/lúc' cho mọi thứ — tiếng Anh phân tay 3 giới từ riêng.
Phương tiện: 'in a car/taxi' nhưng 'on a bus/plane/train'.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi sinh năm 1995.
practice.english: I was born in 1995.

practice.vietnamese: Cuộc họp vào thứ Hai lúc 9 giờ sáng.
practice.english: The meeting is on Monday at 9 AM.

practice.vietnamese: Anh ấy đang ở nhà.
practice.english: He is at home.

lessons.title: Plural Nouns & Uncountables
lessons.description: When to add -s, and which 'logical-feeling-plural' words are actually uncountable.
lessons.rule: Countable + > 1 → add -s/-es. Uncountable (information, advice, water) → never -s.

tldr.rule: Many things → +s. But 'advice', 'information', 'news' are uncountable — say 'a piece of advice'.
tldr.example: She gave me three pieces of advice and lots of useful information.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Cô ấy cho tôi 3 lời khuyên và nhiều thông tin hữu ích.

scenarios.why: Counting items → add -s.
scenarios.english: I bought three books and two pens.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi mua 3 quyển sách và 2 cây bút.

scenarios.why: 'Advice' is uncountable — no 'an advice'.
scenarios.english: Can I get some advice?
scenarios.vietnamese: Cho tôi xin lời khuyên được không?

scenarios.why: 'News' ends in -s but is singular → 'is', not 'are'.
scenarios.english: The news is shocking today.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tin tức hôm nay gây sốc.

scenarios.why: Irregular plural — child → children.
scenarios.english: My two children play piano.
scenarios.vietnamese: Hai con tôi chơi piano.

quickChecks.question: I have two ___.
quickChecks.explanation: Regular plural → just add -s.

quickChecks.question: She gave me ___ advice.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — use 'some', 'a lot of', or 'a piece of'.

quickChecks.question: Three ___ are playing.
quickChecks.explanation: Irregular plural: child → children.

quickChecks.question: The news ___ shocking.
quickChecks.explanation: 'News' looks plural but acts singular.

sections.heading: Regular plurals
sections.body: Add -s for most nouns. Spelling shifts for endings -s/-sh/-ch/-x/-o (+es) and consonant + y (y → ies).
bullets: book → books, dog → dogs
box → boxes, watch → watches
baby → babies
Irregulars: man/men, woman/women, child/children, foot/feet, tooth/teeth, person/people

sections.heading: Common uncountable nouns
sections.body: No -s, no a/an, takes singular verb. Count them with units.
bullets: Liquids/materials: water, milk, rice
Abstract: information, advice, news, work, homework
Units: a glass of water, a piece of advice, a slice of bread

sections.heading: False plurals — end in -s but singular
sections.body: Don't be fooled by the spelling.

examples.english: The news is bad today.
Mathematics is my favorite subject.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt không có hình thức số nhiều — người Việt thường quên thêm -s.
'Information', 'advice', 'news' KHÔNG đếm được — đừng nói 'an advice'.

commonMistakes.wrong: She gave me a good advice.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi có ba quyển sách.
practice.english: I have three books.

practice.vietnamese: Cô ấy cho tôi nhiều lời khuyên.
practice.english: She gave me a lot of advice.

practice.vietnamese: Hai đứa trẻ đang chơi.
practice.english: Two children are playing.

lessons.title: Pronouns: I, me, my, mine
lessons.description: Subject vs object pronouns, possessive forms, and reflexive — pick the right one in one second.
lessons.rule: Before verb → I, he, she. After verb/preposition → me, him, her. Possessive → my (before noun), mine (alone).
examples: This is my book = This book is mine.

tldr.rule: Subject (I/he) before verb. Object (me/him) after verb or preposition. Always 'between you and me', never 'and I'.
tldr.example: My friend and I went to the park. She gave gifts to my friend and me.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Bạn tôi và tôi đi công viên. Cô ấy tặng quà cho bạn tôi và tôi.

scenarios.why: After 'with', use object pronoun.
scenarios.english: Come with me to the cafe.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đi cà phê với tôi đi.

scenarios.why: Possessive adjective (my) before noun, possessive pronoun (mine) alone.
scenarios.english: That's my room. The room next door is hers.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đó là phòng của tôi. Phòng bên cạnh là của cô ấy.

scenarios.why: Reflexive pronoun emphasizes 'no help from anyone'.
scenarios.english: I built this website myself.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi tự xây trang web này một mình.

scenarios.why: 'Between you and me' — never 'between you and I'.
scenarios.english: This is between you and me.
scenarios.vietnamese: Chuyện này chỉ giữa bạn và tôi.

quickChecks.question: He went to the cafe with ___.
quickChecks.explanation: After preposition 'with' → object pronoun 'me'.

quickChecks.question: This book is ___.
quickChecks.explanation: No noun after it → possessive pronoun 'mine'.

quickChecks.question: She introduced ___ to the audience.
quickChecks.explanation: Subject and object are the same person → reflexive 'herself'.

quickChecks.question: ___ went to school.
quickChecks.explanation: Subject of the sentence → 'I' (and place yourself last for politeness).

sections.heading: Subject vs Object
sections.body: Subject pronoun starts the action. Object pronoun receives it.
bullets: Subject: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
Object: me, you, him, her, it, us, them
After every preposition → object form

sections.heading: Possessive adjective vs pronoun
sections.body: Adjective sits before a noun. Pronoun stands alone.
bullets: Adjective: my, your, his, her, its, our, their + noun
Pronoun: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs (alone)

sections.heading: Reflexive — when subject = object
sections.body: Use -self/-selves when the doer and receiver are the same person.

examples.english: I cut myself.
They taught themselves coding.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt dùng 'tôi/của tôi' cho mọi vị trí. Tiếng Anh phân biệt rõ → sau giới từ luôn dùng me, không I.

commonMistakes.explanation: Subject → I, và đặt mình sau.

practice.vietnamese: Anh ấy đi với chúng tôi.
practice.english: He went with us.

practice.vietnamese: Đây là điện thoại của tôi.
practice.english: This is my phone.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi tự làm nó.
practice.english: I did it myself.

lessons.title: Comparatives & Superlatives
lessons.description: Faster, fastest. More beautiful, most beautiful. Pick the right form by syllable count.
lessons.rule: 1-syllable → +er/+est. 3+ syllables → more/most. 2-syllable: depends on ending.

tldr.rule: Short adj → +er/+est. Long adj → more/most. Never combine: 'more taller' is wrong.
tldr.example: She runs faster than me, but he's the most consistent runner.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Cô ấy chạy nhanh hơn tôi, nhưng anh ấy chạy đều nhất.

scenarios.why: Comparing 2 things → comparative + 'than'.
scenarios.english: Lan is taller than Mai.
scenarios.vietnamese: Lan cao hơn Mai.

scenarios.context: 🏆 Picking the best of a group
scenarios.why: Comparing 3+ → superlative with 'the'.
scenarios.english: She is the smartest student in the class.
scenarios.vietnamese: Cô ấy là học sinh thông minh nhất lớp.

scenarios.why: Use comparative with 'than' for direct comparison.
scenarios.english: Coffee here is more expensive than at home.
scenarios.vietnamese: Cà phê ở đây đắt hơn ở nhà.

scenarios.why: Irregular: good → better → best. No 'more good'.
scenarios.english: This is the best film of the year.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đây là phim hay nhất năm.

quickChecks.question: She is ___ than me.
quickChecks.explanation: 1-syllable adj → +er. Never combine 'more' with '-er'.

quickChecks.question: This is ___ book I have ever read.
quickChecks.explanation: Superlative of 'good' is 'best', and we say 'the best'.

quickChecks.question: English is ___ than Vietnamese for me.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Difficult' is long (3 syllables) → use 'more'.

quickChecks.question: She is ___ in our group.
quickChecks.explanation: Comparing more than 2 people in a group → superlative.

sections.heading: Short adj — +er / +est
sections.body: 1-syllable and many 2-syllable adjectives.
bullets: Default: +er/+est (tall → taller → tallest)
Ends in -e: +r/+st (large → larger → largest)
Consonant + y: y → ier/iest (happy → happier → happiest)
CVC pattern: double the consonant (big → bigger → biggest)

sections.heading: Long adj — more / most
sections.body: 3+ syllables and most 2-syllable adjectives.

examples.english: more interesting → most interesting
the most talented person

sections.heading: Irregulars — memorize
sections.body: These don't follow the pattern.
bullets: good → better → best
bad → worse → worst
far → farther/further → farthest/furthest
little → less → least
many/much → more → most

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt 'hơn'/'nhất' đứng SAU adj. Tiếng Anh thêm đuôi hoặc more/most TRƯỚC adj.
KHÔNG kết hợp 'more' với '-er': 'more taller' SAI.

commonMistakes.wrong: She is more taller than me.
This is the most good book.

commonMistakes.right: She is the most beautiful girl.

practice.vietnamese: Anh ấy nhanh hơn tôi.
practice.english: He is faster than me.

practice.vietnamese: Đây là cuốn sách hay nhất tôi từng đọc.
practice.english: This is the best book I have ever read.

practice.vietnamese: Tiếng Anh khó hơn tiếng Việt.
practice.english: English is more difficult than Vietnamese.

lessons.title: Modal Verbs: can, should, must, may
lessons.description: Modals add flavor: ability, obligation, advice, possibility. Mix them up and your sentence means something different.
lessons.rule: Modal + base verb (no 'to', no -s, no -ing). Choose by intent: ability (can), advice (should), obligation (must), possibility (may).

tldr.rule: Pick by intent: CAN (can do) · SHOULD (advice) · MUST (obligation) · MAY (possibility). Always + base verb.
tldr.example: You should see a doctor. You must rest. It may help.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Bạn nên đi khám. Bạn phải nghỉ ngơi. Có thể sẽ đỡ.

scenarios.why: 'Could you' is more polite than 'can you'.
scenarios.english: Could you help me with this?
scenarios.vietnamese: Bạn có thể giúp tôi việc này không?

scenarios.why: 'Should' is for suggestions and recommendations.
scenarios.english: You should drink more water.
scenarios.vietnamese: Bạn nên uống nhiều nước hơn.

scenarios.why: 'Must' for strong obligation (rules, laws).
scenarios.english: You must stop at red lights.
scenarios.vietnamese: Bạn phải dừng khi đèn đỏ.

scenarios.why: 'May/might' = possibility, not certainty.
scenarios.english: It might rain this afternoon.
scenarios.vietnamese: Chiều nay có thể mưa.

quickChecks.question: She ___ swim very well.
quickChecks.explanation: Modal verb: no -s, no 'to'. Just 'can swim'.

quickChecks.question: You ___ smoke in this building. It's against the rules.
quickChecks.explanation: Strict prohibition → 'mustn't'. 'Don't have to' means 'not necessary', different meaning.

quickChecks.question: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.
quickChecks.explanation: Friendly advice → 'should'.

quickChecks.question: ___ I borrow your pen?
quickChecks.explanation: Polite request for permission → 'May I…?'

sections.heading: Can / Could — ability & permission
sections.body: Can = present ability. Could = past ability or polite request.

examples.english: I can speak English.
Could you help me?

sections.heading: Must / Have to — obligation
sections.body: Must = internal sense of duty or strict rule. Have to = external obligation.
bullets: Mustn't = strictly forbidden (You mustn't smoke here)
Don't have to = not required (different from mustn't!)

sections.heading: Should — advice
sections.body: Friendly suggestion, weaker than must.

examples.english: You should see a doctor.
We shouldn't waste water.

sections.heading: May / Might — possibility
sections.body: Something is possible but not certain.

examples.english: It may rain tomorrow.
She might come to the party.

vietnameseTips: Modal verbs KHÔNG thêm -s, KHÔNG đi với 'to'. Sai phổ biến: 'She cans speak' → đúng 'She can speak'.
'Mustn't' (cấm) ≠ 'don't have to' (không cần). Phân biệt rõ.

commonMistakes.wrong: You don't have to smoke here.

practice.vietnamese: Bạn có thể giúp tôi mở cửa không?
practice.english: Could you help me open the door?

practice.vietnamese: Anh ấy nên đi ngủ sớm.
practice.english: He should go to bed early.

practice.vietnamese: Trời có thể mưa chiều nay.
practice.english: It may rain this afternoon.

lessons.title: Conditionals (if-clauses)
lessons.description: Real, possible, imaginary, regret — 4 types of 'if' for 4 different feelings.
lessons.rule: Each conditional pairs a tense in the if-clause with a tense in the result. Mix correctly or the meaning shifts.
examples: If water boils, it evaporates. (zero — fact)
If it rains, I will stay home. (first — likely)
If I were rich, I would travel. (second — imagined)
If I had studied, I would have passed. (third — past regret)

tldr.rule: Ask: how real is it? Fact → zero. Likely → first. Imagined now → second. Past regret → third.
tldr.example: If I were you, I would apologize. (you're not me, but imagining)
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ xin lỗi. (giả định)

scenarios.why: Likely future event → first conditional.
scenarios.english: If it rains tomorrow, I'll bring an umbrella.
scenarios.vietnamese: Nếu mai trời mưa, tôi sẽ mang ô.

scenarios.why: Imagining something not true → second conditional with 'were'.
scenarios.english: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
scenarios.vietnamese: Nếu tôi trúng số, tôi sẽ đi du lịch khắp thế giới.

scenarios.why: Past possibility that didn't happen → third conditional.
scenarios.english: If I had studied harder, I would have passed.
scenarios.vietnamese: Nếu tôi học chăm hơn, tôi đã đậu rồi.

scenarios.why: Always-true cause-effect → zero conditional, present tense both sides.
scenarios.english: If you heat ice, it melts.
scenarios.vietnamese: Nếu bạn đun đá, nó tan.

quickChecks.question: If it ___ tomorrow, I will stay home.
quickChecks.explanation: First conditional: if + present, result + will. Never 'will' in the if-clause.

quickChecks.question: If I ___ you, I would tell the truth.
quickChecks.explanation: Second conditional traditionally uses 'were' for all subjects (formal/standard).

quickChecks.question: If she had known, she ___ helped.
quickChecks.explanation: Third conditional: if + had + V3, result = would have + V3.

quickChecks.question: If you heat water to 100°C, it ___.
quickChecks.explanation: Zero conditional (universal fact): both sides in present simple.

sections.heading: Zero — facts
sections.body: If + present, present. For scientific facts and rules.

examples.english: If you heat ice, it melts.

sections.heading: First — likely future
sections.body: If + present, will + base. For things that may actually happen.
bullets: Never use 'will' in the if-clause
Can swap 'will' for can/may/should depending on certainty

sections.heading: Second — imagined now
sections.body: If + past, would + base. For unreal or unlikely present situations.

examples.english: If I were rich, I would buy a house.
examples.note: 'Were' for all subjects in formal English.

sections.heading: Third — regret about past
sections.body: If + had + V3, would have + V3. About what could have happened but didn't.

examples.english: If I had studied, I would have passed.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt 'nếu… thì…' không phân biệt thực tế hay tưởng tượng — tiếng Anh chia tense.
Second/third conditional dùng 'were' (không 'was') cho mọi ngôi (chuẩn).

commonMistakes.wrong: If it will rain, I will stay home.
commonMistakes.right: If it rains, I will stay home.

commonMistakes.wrong: If I had studied, I would pass.
commonMistakes.right: If I had studied, I would have passed.

practice.vietnamese: Nếu trời mưa, tôi sẽ mang ô.
practice.english: If it rains, I will bring an umbrella.

practice.vietnamese: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ học chăm hơn.
practice.english: If I were you, I would study harder.

practice.vietnamese: Nếu tôi biết, tôi đã giúp bạn rồi.
practice.english: If I had known, I would have helped you.

lessons.title: Passive Voice
lessons.description: Shift the focus from doer to receiver. Use it when WHO doesn't matter — or matters less than WHAT.
lessons.rule: Passive = be + V3 (past participle). The original object becomes the new subject.
examples: They build houses. → Houses are built.
She wrote the book. → The book was written by her.

tldr.rule: Use when the doer is unknown, obvious, or unimportant. Form: be (matching tense) + V3.
tldr.example: My wallet was stolen. (We don't know who.)
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Ví của tôi bị trộm. (Không biết ai.)

scenarios.why: Doer unknown → passive.
scenarios.english: My bike was stolen last night.
scenarios.vietnamese: Xe đạp của tôi bị trộm tối qua.

scenarios.why: Builder name is less important than the building itself.
scenarios.english: The Sydney Opera House was designed in 1957.
scenarios.vietnamese: Nhà hát Opera Sydney được thiết kế năm 1957.

scenarios.why: Subject is universal — saying everyone speaks English globally.
scenarios.english: English is spoken in over 50 countries.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tiếng Anh được nói ở hơn 50 quốc gia.

scenarios.why: Focus on the steps, not the workers.
scenarios.english: The package is delivered within 3 days.
scenarios.vietnamese: Hàng được giao trong 3 ngày.

quickChecks.question: The book ___ by Hemingway.
quickChecks.explanation: Past passive: was + V3 (written, not wrote).

quickChecks.question: My wallet ___ yesterday.
quickChecks.explanation: Past passive of 'steal' → was stolen.

quickChecks.question: The work ___ tomorrow.
quickChecks.explanation: Future passive: will be + V3.

quickChecks.question: English ___ everywhere.
quickChecks.explanation: Present passive: am/is/are + V3.

sections.heading: Forming passive — match the tense
sections.body: Conjugate 'be' to match the tense, then add V3.
bullets: Present: is/are + V3 → 'Coffee is grown in Brazil'
Past: was/were + V3 → 'The cake was eaten'
Present perfect: has/have been + V3
Future: will be + V3
Modal: modal + be + V3 → 'It must be done'

sections.heading: When to use passive
sections.body: Pick passive when the doer doesn't matter, is unknown, or is obvious.

examples.english: My wallet was stolen.
English is spoken worldwide.

sections.heading: Use 'by' only when relevant
sections.body: Mention the doer only if it adds meaning.

examples.english: The novel was written by Hemingway.
The bridge was built in 1990.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt 'được/bị' không luôn = passive trong tiếng Anh. 'Tôi bị mất ví' = 'I lost my wallet' chứ không phải 'I was lost my wallet'.

commonMistakes.wrong: The book is wrote by him.
commonMistakes.right: The book is written by him.

commonMistakes.wrong: My wallet was stolen by someone.
commonMistakes.explanation: Tác nhân không cụ thể → bỏ 'by'.

commonMistakes.wrong: The work will be do tomorrow.
commonMistakes.right: The work will be done tomorrow.

practice.vietnamese: Cuốn sách này được viết năm 1990.
practice.english: This book was written in 1990.

practice.vietnamese: Tiếng Anh được dạy ở khắp nơi.
practice.english: English is taught everywhere.

practice.vietnamese: Dự án đã được hoàn thành.
practice.english: The project has been finished.

lessons.title: Word Order
lessons.description: Subject-Verb-Object is fixed. Where do adverbs go? How do adjectives stack? Master the order so your English sounds natural.
lessons.rule: S+V+O. Frequency adverbs before main verb, after 'be'. Multiple adjectives follow OSASCOMP order.
examples: a beautiful big old red wooden table

tldr.rule: Adverbs of frequency before normal verb, after 'be'. Adjectives: opinion → size → age → color → origin → material → noun.
tldr.example: She is always late. I bought a beautiful small red Vietnamese basket.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Cô ấy luôn đến muộn. Tôi mua một cái giỏ Việt Nam nhỏ xinh màu đỏ.

scenarios.why: Frequency adverb (always/often/never) before the main verb.
scenarios.english: I always check my email first thing.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi luôn kiểm tra email đầu tiên.

scenarios.why: Stack adjectives in OSASCOMP order — opinion comes first.
scenarios.english: She wore a pretty long silk dress.
scenarios.vietnamese: Cô ấy mặc một cái váy lụa dài đẹp.

scenarios.why: Manner adverb after the object, not between verb and object.
scenarios.english: He speaks English fluently.
scenarios.vietnamese: Anh ấy nói tiếng Anh trôi chảy.

scenarios.why: Indirect + direct object order: give someone something.
scenarios.english: I gave my friend a book.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi tặng bạn tôi một quyển sách.

quickChecks.question: I ___ to the gym.
quickChecks.explanation: Frequency adverb 'always' goes BEFORE the main verb.

quickChecks.question: She speaks ___.
quickChecks.explanation: Manner adverb 'well' goes after the object 'English'.

quickChecks.question: I bought a ___ car.
quickChecks.explanation: Size comes before color in OSASCOMP order.

quickChecks.question: She is ___ late.
quickChecks.explanation: After 'be', frequency adverb comes RIGHT AFTER: 'She is never late'.

sections.heading: Basic word order
sections.body: Subject + Verb + Object is fixed. Vietnamese is more flexible, English is not.

examples.english: I love you.
examples.vietnamese: Tôi yêu bạn.

examples.english: She gave me a book.
examples.note: S + V + indirect O + direct O

sections.heading: Frequency adverbs
sections.body: Always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never.
bullets: Before the main verb: I always brush my teeth.
After 'be': She is never late.
After modals: We can usually finish on time.

sections.heading: Adjective order — OSASCOMP
sections.body: Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Color → Origin → Material → Purpose → Noun.

examples.english: a beautiful small old round red Vietnamese wooden cooking pot
a nice young Vietnamese woman

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt: tính từ đứng SAU danh từ ('nhà to'). Tiếng Anh: TRƯỚC ('a big house').
Có nhiều tính từ? OSASCOMP order, hoặc đơn giản hơn: tách thành 2 câu.

commonMistakes.explanation: Trạng từ cách thức sau tân ngữ.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi luôn ăn sáng lúc 7 giờ.
practice.english: I always have breakfast at 7.

practice.vietnamese: Cô ấy là một cô gái Việt Nam xinh đẹp.
practice.english: She is a beautiful Vietnamese girl.

practice.vietnamese: Anh ấy nói tiếng Anh rất giỏi.
practice.english: He speaks English very well.

lessons.title: Relative Clauses
lessons.description: Who, which, that, whose, where — add information to a noun without starting a new sentence.
lessons.rule: Who = people. Which = things. That = either (in defining clauses only). Whose = possession. Where = place.
examples: The man who lives next door is friendly.
The book which I bought is interesting.
The city where I was born is Hanoi.

tldr.rule: Who for people, which for things, that for either. Commas → non-defining (extra info, can drop).
tldr.example: My brother, who lives in Hanoi, is a doctor.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Anh tôi, sống ở Hà Nội, là bác sĩ.

scenarios.why: Add info about a person → 'who'.
scenarios.english: This is Lan, who works with me.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đây là Lan, đồng nghiệp tôi.

scenarios.why: Identify which specific book → defining clause, no commas.
scenarios.english: The book that I recommended is on the table.
scenarios.vietnamese: Cuốn sách tôi giới thiệu nằm trên bàn.

scenarios.why: Reference a place → 'where'.
scenarios.english: This is the town where I grew up.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đây là thị trấn tôi lớn lên.

scenarios.why: Possession → 'whose'.
scenarios.english: I have a friend whose mom is a chef.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi có một người bạn có mẹ là đầu bếp.

quickChecks.question: The book ___ I read was great.
quickChecks.explanation: Book is a thing → 'which' (or 'that').

quickChecks.question: The man ___ called me is my uncle.
quickChecks.explanation: Man is a person → 'who'.

quickChecks.question: This is the school ___ I studied.
quickChecks.explanation: Location → 'where'.

quickChecks.question: I met a woman ___ son is famous.
quickChecks.explanation: Possession (the woman's son) → 'whose'.

sections.heading: Defining vs Non-defining
sections.body: Defining = essential info, no commas. Non-defining = extra info, commas both sides.

examples.english: The man who called you is my friend.
My father, who lives in Hanoi, is a doctor.

bullets: Defining: no commas, 'that' is OK
Non-defining: commas both sides, NEVER 'that'

sections.heading: When to drop the pronoun
sections.body: If who/which/that is the OBJECT of a defining clause, you can drop it.

examples.english: The book (that) I bought is interesting.
The man who called me is here.

sections.heading: Whose & Where
sections.body: Special cases for possession and location.

examples.english: I met a woman whose son is famous.
This is the school where I studied.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt dùng 'mà' cho cả người và vật. Tiếng Anh phân biệt who (người) vs which (vật).
'That' KHÔNG dùng trong non-defining clause (có dấu phẩy).

commonMistakes.wrong: My mother that lives in HCMC is a teacher.
commonMistakes.right: My mother, who lives in HCMC, is a teacher.

practice.vietnamese: Người phụ nữ đang ngồi đó là cô tôi.
practice.english: The woman who is sitting there is my aunt.

practice.vietnamese: Bộ phim tôi xem hôm qua rất hay.
practice.english: The movie (that) I watched yesterday was great.

practice.vietnamese: Đây là thành phố tôi lớn lên.
practice.english: This is the city where I grew up.

lessons.title: Asking Questions
lessons.description: Yes/no questions, Wh- questions, and the auxiliary verb that Vietnamese doesn't need but English always does.
lessons.rule: Put an auxiliary (do/does/did, be, have, can…) before the subject. The Wh- word goes first.

tldr.rule: (Wh- word) + auxiliary + subject + main verb. No auxiliary, no question.
tldr.example: Where do you live? What time does the shop open?
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Bạn sống ở đâu? Cửa hàng mở cửa lúc mấy giờ?

scenarios.why: Polite requests put 'Can/Could' before the subject.
scenarios.english: Could I have an iced milk coffee, please?
scenarios.vietnamese: Cho tôi một ly cà phê sữa đá nhé?

scenarios.why: Wh- word + does + subject + base verb.
scenarios.english: Excuse me, where does this bus go?
scenarios.vietnamese: Xin lỗi, xe buýt này đi đâu vậy?

scenarios.why: Past questions use 'did' + base verb.
scenarios.english: How did you hear about this position?
scenarios.vietnamese: Bạn biết đến vị trí này bằng cách nào?

scenarios.why: With 'be', just swap the subject and the verb.
scenarios.english: Are you free this weekend?
scenarios.vietnamese: Cuối tuần này bạn rảnh không?

quickChecks.question: ___ she speak Japanese?
quickChecks.explanation: Main verb 'speak', subject 'she', present tense → 'Does'.

quickChecks.question: Where ___ you go last night?
quickChecks.explanation: 'Last night' is past; main verb 'go' → 'did' + base form.

quickChecks.question: What ___ you doing right now?
quickChecks.explanation: 'Doing' is present continuous → the auxiliary is 'are'.

quickChecks.question: Which question is correct?
quickChecks.explanation: Wh- word + be + subject: 'Why are you late?'

sections.heading: Yes/No questions — move the auxiliary to the front
sections.body: If the sentence already has be, can, will, or have (perfect tense), move it before the subject. If there is no auxiliary, add do/does/did.
bullets: She is tired. → Is she tired?
You can swim. → Can you swim?
They live here. → Do they live here?
He works late. → Does he work late? (the -s moves to 'does')

examples.english: Have you finished your homework?
examples.vietnamese: Bạn làm xong bài tập chưa?

examples.english: Did you sleep well?
examples.vietnamese: Bạn ngủ có ngon không?
examples.note: After 'did', the main verb is the base form: sleep, NOT slept.

sections.heading: Wh- questions — remember QASI
sections.body: Question word + Auxiliary + Subject + Infinitive (base verb).
bullets: What / Where / When / Why / Who / How + auxiliary + subject + verb
How much / How many / How long / How often follow the same order

examples.english: What time do you usually get up?
examples.vietnamese: Bạn thường dậy lúc mấy giờ?

examples.english: How long have you lived in Da Nang?
examples.vietnamese: Bạn sống ở Đà Nẵng được bao lâu rồi?

sections.heading: Subject questions — no do/does/did
sections.body: When who or what is the SUBJECT (the one doing the action), keep normal word order and don't add an auxiliary.

examples.english: Who called you?
Who did you call?
examples.note: Who = the person you called (object) → 'did' is needed.

examples.english: What happened?
examples.vietnamese: Chuyện gì đã xảy ra vậy?

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt tạo câu hỏi bằng cách thêm 'không', 'chưa', 'à' vào cuối câu ('Bạn thích cà phê không?'). Tiếng Anh phải đưa trợ động từ lên trước chủ ngữ: 'Do you like coffee?'.
Từ để hỏi trong tiếng Việt thường đứng cuối câu ('Bạn sống ở đâu?'), còn tiếng Anh luôn đưa từ để hỏi lên đầu: 'Where do you live?'.
Đã dùng do/does/did thì động từ chính phải về nguyên thể: 'Does she like…?' chứ không phải 'Does she likes…?'.

commonMistakes.explanation: Câu hỏi cần trợ động từ 'do' đứng trước chủ ngữ.
Sau từ để hỏi phải có trợ động từ + chủ ngữ.
'Did' đã mang thì quá khứ → động từ chính dùng nguyên thể.

practice.vietnamese: Bạn làm việc ở đâu?
practice.english: Where do you work?

practice.vietnamese: Hôm qua anh ấy có gọi cho bạn không?
practice.english: Did he call you yesterday?

practice.vietnamese: Ai đã làm vỡ cái cốc?
practice.english: Who broke the glass?

lessons.title: Future Forms: will, going to, present continuous
lessons.description: Three everyday ways to talk about the future — and how to choose between a quick decision, a plan, and a fixed arrangement.
lessons.rule: Will = decided now or a prediction from opinion. Going to = plan already made or visible evidence. Present continuous = fixed arrangement.
examples: I'm thirsty. I'll get some water.
I'm going to learn Korean next year.
Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
I'm meeting my boss at 3 p.m. tomorrow.

tldr.rule: Decide now → will. Already planned → going to. Booked with a time → present continuous.
tldr.example: The phone's ringing — I'll get it! I'm going to visit Hue in May.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Điện thoại reo kìa — để tôi nghe! Tháng Năm tôi định đi Huế.

scenarios.why: An offer decided at the moment of speaking → will.
scenarios.english: Don't worry, I'll send you the file now.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đừng lo, tôi gửi file cho bạn ngay.

scenarios.why: An intention you already have → going to.
scenarios.english: I'm going to take the IELTS test in December.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi định thi IELTS vào tháng Mười Hai.

scenarios.why: Arranged with other people at a fixed time → present continuous.
scenarios.english: We're having dinner with my parents on Saturday.
scenarios.vietnamese: Thứ Bảy này chúng tôi ăn tối với bố mẹ tôi.

scenarios.why: You can see the signs right now → going to.
scenarios.english: Slow down! You're going to hit that motorbike.
scenarios.vietnamese: Chạy chậm lại! Bạn sắp đâm vào chiếc xe máy kia rồi.

quickChecks.question: A: We've run out of milk. B: OK, I ___ buy some.
quickChecks.explanation: B decides at the moment of speaking → 'will'.

quickChecks.question: She has already bought a ticket. She ___ fly to Seoul next week.
quickChecks.explanation: The plan was made before (ticket bought) → 'is going to'.

quickChecks.question: I ___ my dentist at 10 a.m. tomorrow — it's booked.
quickChecks.explanation: Fixed arrangement with a time → present continuous.

quickChecks.question: I think Vietnam ___ win the match.
quickChecks.explanation: A prediction based on opinion ('I think') → 'will'.

sections.heading: Will — instant decisions, offers, promises, opinions
sections.body: Use will + base verb when you decide at the moment of speaking, make an offer or promise, or predict from your opinion.
bullets: Common with: I think, probably, I'm sure, maybe
Negative: won't (= will not)

examples.english: I'll call you back in five minutes.
examples.vietnamese: Năm phút nữa tôi gọi lại cho bạn.

examples.english: I'm sure you won't fail.
examples.vietnamese: Tôi chắc là bạn sẽ không trượt đâu.

sections.heading: Be going to — plans and visible evidence
sections.body: Use am/is/are going to + base verb for intentions decided before speaking, or predictions based on what you can see now.
bullets: Form: am/is/are + going to + base verb
In fast speech 'going to' sounds like 'gonna' — don't write 'gonna' in formal writing

examples.english: We're going to move to a bigger apartment.
examples.vietnamese: Chúng tôi định chuyển đến một căn hộ rộng hơn.

examples.english: The sky is very dark. It's going to storm.

sections.heading: Present continuous — fixed arrangements
sections.body: Use am/is/are + V-ing for future plans already arranged with other people, usually with a time or place.

examples.english: I'm flying to Phu Quoc on Friday.
examples.vietnamese: Thứ Sáu tôi bay đi Phú Quốc.

examples.english: What are you doing tonight?
examples.vietnamese: Tối nay bạn làm gì?

vietnameseTips: Mẹo nhớ: quyết định ngay lúc nói → 'will'; 'định làm gì' (đã tính từ trước) → 'going to'; đã hẹn giờ, đặt chỗ → hiện tại tiếp diễn.
Đừng dịch máy móc mọi chữ 'sẽ' thành 'will'. 'Tuần sau tôi sẽ đi Đà Lạt' (đã đặt vé) nên nói 'I'm going to Da Lat next week.'
Sau 'will' và 'going to' luôn là động từ nguyên thể: 'will go', 'going to go' — không phải 'will going' hay 'going to went'.

commonMistakes.right: She is going to study abroad.

commonMistakes.wrong: A: This bag is so heavy. B: I'm going to help you.
commonMistakes.right: A: This bag is so heavy. B: I'll help you.
commonMistakes.explanation: Lời đề nghị giúp đỡ quyết định ngay lúc nói → dùng 'will'.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi định học thạc sĩ ở Úc.
practice.english: I'm going to do a master's degree in Australia.

practice.vietnamese: Để tôi mở cửa cho.
practice.english: I'll open the door for you.

practice.vietnamese: Tối mai chúng tôi gặp khách hàng lúc 7 giờ.
practice.english: We're meeting a client at 7 tomorrow evening.

lessons.title: Quantifiers: much, many, a few, a little
lessons.description: Choose the right 'how much' word by asking one question first: can I count it?
lessons.rule: Many / a few / few + plural countable nouns. Much / a little / little + uncountable nouns. A lot of, some, and any work with both.
examples: How many students are in your class?
I have a few friends in Hanoi.
Can I have a little sugar?

tldr.rule: Countable → many / a few. Uncountable → much / a little. Not sure? 'A lot of' fits both.
tldr.example: There are many motorbikes but not much space.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Có rất nhiều xe máy nhưng không có nhiều chỗ trống.

scenarios.why: How many → countable items; how much → uncountable amounts or prices.
scenarios.english: How many mangoes do you want, and how much rice?
scenarios.vietnamese: Bạn muốn mấy quả xoài, và bao nhiêu gạo?

scenarios.why: A small amount of something uncountable → a little.
scenarios.english: Just a little chili, please.
scenarios.vietnamese: Cho tôi ít ớt thôi nhé.

scenarios.why: A small positive number of countable things → a few.
scenarios.english: I've made a few friends at work already.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi đã có được vài người bạn ở chỗ làm rồi.

scenarios.why: Negative sentence + uncountable noun → not much.
scenarios.english: Sorry, I don't have much time today.
scenarios.vietnamese: Xin lỗi, hôm nay tôi không có nhiều thời gian.

quickChecks.question: There aren't ___ people here today.
quickChecks.explanation: 'People' is plural and countable → 'many'.

quickChecks.question: We need ___ information before we decide.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable; 'some' works with uncountable nouns.

quickChecks.question: I have ___ money left, so I can buy you a coffee.
quickChecks.explanation: Positive meaning (enough for coffee) + uncountable → 'a little'.

quickChecks.question: Very ___ students passed the test, so the teacher was disappointed.
quickChecks.explanation: Countable + negative meaning (almost none) → 'few'.

sections.heading: Countable vs uncountable — the first question
sections.body: Countable nouns have singular and plural forms (one book, two books). Uncountable nouns have no plural and no a/an (water, advice, furniture, homework).
bullets: Countable only: many, a few, few, a number of
Uncountable only: much, a little, little, a great deal of
Both: a lot of / lots of, some, any, no, enough

examples.english: How many cups of coffee do you drink a day?
examples.note: You count the cups, not the coffee.

examples.english: There's a lot of traffic and a lot of cars.
examples.vietnamese: Đường rất đông và có rất nhiều ô tô.

sections.heading: Much / many in positive sentences
sections.body: In everyday English, much and many sound most natural in questions and negatives. In positive sentences, 'a lot of' is more common.

examples.english: Do you have much homework? — Yes, I have a lot of homework.
examples.vietnamese: Bạn có nhiều bài tập không? — Có, nhiều lắm.

examples.english: She doesn't eat much meat.
examples.vietnamese: Cô ấy không ăn nhiều thịt.

sections.heading: A few vs few, a little vs little
sections.body: With 'a', the meaning is positive (some, enough). Without 'a', the meaning is negative (almost none, not enough).
bullets: a few / a little = some, enough to be useful
few / little = almost none, not enough

examples.english: I have a few ideas. Let's discuss them.
He had few ideas, so the meeting was short.
There's little hope of finding the wallet now.
examples.vietnamese: Giờ thì hầu như không còn hy vọng tìm lại được cái ví.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt chỉ có 'nhiều' và 'ít' cho mọi danh từ, nên hãy tự hỏi 'có đếm được không?' trước khi chọn many/much hay a few/a little.
Nhiều danh từ tiếng Việt đếm được nhưng tiếng Anh lại không đếm được: advice, information, homework, luggage, furniture, news. Chúng đi với 'much', 'a little' và không thêm -s.
Mẹo: có 'a' là nghĩa tích cực ('vẫn còn một ít'), không có 'a' là nghĩa tiêu cực ('chẳng còn bao nhiêu').

commonMistakes.wrong: There are much people in the park.
commonMistakes.right: There are many people in the park.
commonMistakes.explanation: 'People' là danh từ số nhiều đếm được → many (hoặc a lot of).

commonMistakes.wrong: Can you give me some advices?
commonMistakes.right: Can you give me some advice?

commonMistakes.wrong: I have little friends, so I'm never lonely.
commonMistakes.right: I have a few friends, so I'm never lonely.
commonMistakes.explanation: Danh từ đếm được + nghĩa tích cực → 'a few'. 'Little' dùng cho danh từ không đếm được.

practice.vietnamese: Bạn có bao nhiêu anh chị em?
practice.english: How many brothers and sisters do you have?

practice.vietnamese: Tôi không uống nhiều cà phê.
practice.english: I don't drink much coffee.

practice.vietnamese: Chúng ta còn một chút thời gian, uống trà nhé.
practice.english: We have a little time left, so let's have some tea.

lessons.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
lessons.description: Both talk about the past — the difference is whether the time is finished and stated, or still connected to now.
lessons.rule: Past simple = finished time (yesterday, in 2019, ago). Present perfect = no specific time, or a period that continues to now.
examples: She has worked here since March.
She worked there for two years, then left.

tldr.rule: Can you name a finished time? Past simple. No finished time, or still true? Present perfect.
tldr.example: I've lost my keys! I think I dropped them on the bus.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Tôi làm mất chìa khóa rồi! Chắc tôi đánh rơi trên xe buýt.

scenarios.why: Experience up to now with no time given → present perfect.
scenarios.english: I have managed a team of five people.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi từng quản lý một nhóm năm người.

scenarios.why: A specific, finished trip with details → past simple.
scenarios.english: Last summer we went to Ha Giang and rode motorbikes for three days.
scenarios.vietnamese: Hè năm ngoái chúng tôi đi Hà Giang và chạy xe máy suốt ba ngày.

scenarios.why: News with a present result → present perfect; the details → past simple.
scenarios.english: Guess what? I've got the job! They called me an hour ago.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đoán xem? Tôi được nhận rồi! Họ gọi cho tôi một tiếng trước.

scenarios.why: Started in the past and still true → present perfect + for/since.
scenarios.english: We've lived in this apartment since 2021.
scenarios.vietnamese: Chúng tôi sống ở căn hộ này từ năm 2021.

quickChecks.question: I ___ that film last weekend.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Last weekend' is a finished time → past simple.

quickChecks.question: ___ you ever ___ durian?
quickChecks.explanation: 'Ever' asks about life experience up to now → present perfect.

quickChecks.question: My father ___ for this company for 20 years. He retired in 2015.
quickChecks.explanation: The period is finished (he retired) → past simple.

quickChecks.question: She ___ here since 2020, and she still loves it.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Since' + still true now → present perfect.

sections.heading: Past simple — finished time
sections.body: Use past simple when the action is complete and the time is finished — either stated or clear from the context.
bullets: Signals: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2019, when I was a child
Questions starting with 'When…?' → past simple

examples.english: I met my best friend when I was ten.
examples.vietnamese: Tôi gặp bạn thân năm tôi mười tuổi.

examples.english: When did you arrive?

sections.heading: Present perfect — connected to now
sections.body: Use have/has + past participle when the time is not stated, the time period is still open, or the result matters now.
bullets: Life experience: ever, never, before, twice
Unfinished period: today, this week, so far, recently
Still true: for + length of time, since + starting point
News and results: just, already, yet

examples.english: I've never eaten balut.
examples.vietnamese: Tôi chưa bao giờ ăn trứng vịt lộn.

examples.english: Have you finished the report yet?
examples.vietnamese: Bạn làm xong báo cáo chưa?

sections.heading: The switch: from news to details
sections.body: Native speakers often introduce news with the present perfect, then switch to the past simple for the details.

examples.english: I've broken my phone. I dropped it in the kitchen this morning.
Have you been to Hoi An? — Yes, I went there last year.
examples.vietnamese: Bạn đến Hội An chưa? — Rồi, tôi đi năm ngoái.

sections.heading: For vs since
sections.body: Both are common with the present perfect, but they answer different questions.
bullets: for + a length of time: for three years, for a long time
since + a starting point: since 2020, since Monday, since I was a child

examples.english: I've studied English for six years / since 2019.
examples.vietnamese: Tôi đã học tiếng Anh được sáu năm / từ năm 2019.

vietnameseTips: Chữ 'đã' trong tiếng Việt có thể ứng với cả quá khứ đơn lẫn hiện tại hoàn thành, nên đừng dựa vào 'đã'. Hãy nhìn trạng từ thời gian: có mốc thời gian đã kết thúc → quá khứ đơn.
'Chưa bao giờ', 'từng', '…chưa?' thường ứng với hiện tại hoàn thành: 'Bạn ăn sáng chưa?' → 'Have you had breakfast yet?'.
Câu hỏi bắt đầu bằng 'When' gần như luôn dùng quá khứ đơn: 'When did you start?'.

commonMistakes.explanation: 'In 2020' là mốc thời gian đã kết thúc → quá khứ đơn.
Bắt đầu trong quá khứ và vẫn còn đúng → hiện tại hoàn thành với 'since'.
'When' hỏi về một thời điểm cụ thể → quá khứ đơn.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi đã làm việc ở đây được ba năm.
practice.english: I have worked here for three years.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi gặp anh ấy hai ngày trước.
practice.english: I met him two days ago.

practice.vietnamese: Bạn đã bao giờ đi máy bay chưa?
practice.english: Have you ever been on a plane?

lessons.title: Gerund or Infinitive? (doing vs to do)
lessons.description: Some verbs are followed by -ing, others by to + verb, and a few change meaning. Learn the most useful groups.
lessons.rule: enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, suggest + V-ing. want, decide, hope, plan, agree + to V. After a preposition, always V-ing.
examples: She decided to quit her job.

tldr.rule: Wanting and planning verbs take 'to do'. Enjoy, finish, avoid, and all prepositions take '-ing'.
tldr.example: I want to learn the guitar, and I'm looking forward to starting lessons.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Tôi muốn học đàn guitar và rất mong được bắt đầu học.

scenarios.why: enjoy / don't mind / can't stand → V-ing.
scenarios.english: I really enjoy playing badminton after work.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi rất thích chơi cầu lông sau giờ làm.

scenarios.why: want / plan / hope / decide → to + base verb.
scenarios.english: I'm planning to apply for a scholarship.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi đang dự định nộp hồ sơ xin học bổng.

scenarios.why: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition → V-ing.
scenarios.english: I look forward to hearing from you.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi mong sớm nhận được phản hồi từ anh/chị.

scenarios.why: suggest → V-ing (or 'suggest that…'), never 'suggest to do'.
scenarios.english: I suggest leaving earlier to avoid the traffic.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi đề nghị đi sớm hơn để tránh kẹt xe.

quickChecks.question: Would you mind ___ the window?
quickChecks.explanation: 'Mind' is always followed by V-ing.

quickChecks.question: They agreed ___ the price.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Agree' + to + base verb.

quickChecks.question: She is good at ___ presentations.
quickChecks.explanation: After a preposition ('at') → V-ing.

quickChecks.question: On the way to work, I stopped ___ a coffee.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Stop to do' = pause in order to do something (dừng lại để mua).

sections.heading: Verbs + V-ing
sections.body: These verbs are followed by the -ing form.
bullets: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, keep, practise, suggest, consider, miss, can't stand
Fixed expressions: It's worth…, I can't help…, There's no point (in)…

examples.english: Have you finished writing the report?
examples.vietnamese: Bạn viết xong báo cáo chưa?

examples.english: You should avoid eating late at night.
examples.vietnamese: Bạn nên tránh ăn khuya.

sections.heading: Verbs + to + base verb
sections.body: These verbs are usually about wishes, plans, decisions, and attempts. They are followed by to + base verb.
bullets: want, need, decide, plan, hope, expect, agree, refuse, promise, manage, afford, learn
Verb + person + to V: ask / tell / want / advise someone to do something

examples.english: We can't afford to buy a car yet.
examples.vietnamese: Chúng tôi chưa đủ tiền mua ô tô.

examples.english: My manager asked me to prepare the slides.
examples.vietnamese: Quản lý nhờ tôi chuẩn bị slide.

sections.heading: After prepositions → always V-ing
sections.body: If a preposition (in, on, at, of, about, for, without, before, after) comes before a verb, the verb takes -ing.

examples.english: Thank you for helping me.
examples.vietnamese: Cảm ơn bạn đã giúp tôi.

examples.english: She left without saying goodbye.
I'm used to working late.
examples.note: Here 'to' is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.

sections.heading: Verbs that change meaning
sections.body: A few verbs can take both forms, but the meaning changes.
bullets: stop doing = quit an activity; stop to do = pause in order to do something else
remember doing = recall a past action; remember to do = not forget a task
try doing = experiment to see what happens; try to do = make an effort

examples.english: Remember to lock the door.
examples.note: A task for later — don't forget.

examples.english: I remember locking the door.
examples.note: A memory of a past action.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt đặt hai động từ cạnh nhau rất tự nhiên ('thích nấu ăn', 'muốn đi'), nên người Việt hay quên chọn dạng. Hãy học theo cụm: 'enjoy doing', 'want to do'.
Nhóm 'mong muốn, dự định, quyết định' (want, plan, decide, hope) thường đi với 'to V' vì hướng về tương lai. Nhóm 'thích thú, né tránh, hoàn thành' (enjoy, avoid, finish) đi với 'V-ing'.
'Look forward to', 'be used to', 'object to' có 'to' là giới từ → theo sau là V-ing: 'I look forward to meeting you', không phải 'to meet you'.

commonMistakes.wrong: I enjoy to listen to music.
He suggested to go out for dinner.
commonMistakes.right: He suggested going out for dinner.
commonMistakes.explanation: 'Suggest' + V-ing (hoặc 'suggest that we go…'), không dùng 'to V'.

commonMistakes.wrong: I look forward to meet you.
commonMistakes.right: I look forward to meeting you.
commonMistakes.explanation: 'To' trong 'look forward to' là giới từ → V-ing.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi quyết định học thêm một ngoại ngữ.
practice.english: I decided to learn another foreign language.

practice.vietnamese: Bạn có phiền đợi vài phút không?
practice.english: Do you mind waiting a few minutes?

practice.vietnamese: Cô ấy giỏi giải quyết vấn đề.
practice.english: She is good at solving problems.

lessons.title: Used to vs Be / Get Used to
lessons.description: 'I used to work' and 'I'm used to working' look almost the same but mean very different things.
lessons.rule: used to + base verb = a past habit or state that is no longer true. be/get used to + V-ing/noun = be/become familiar with something.
examples: I used to live in Can Tho.
I'm used to living in a big city now.
It took me months to get used to the cold weather.
Did you use to play football?

tldr.rule: used to + verb = 'trước đây thường'. be used to + V-ing = 'đã quen với'.
tldr.example: I used to hate coffee, but now I'm used to drinking it every morning.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Trước đây tôi ghét cà phê, nhưng giờ tôi đã quen uống nó mỗi sáng.

scenarios.why: Past habits that are no longer true → used to + base verb.
scenarios.english: I used to swim in the river near my grandparents' house.
scenarios.vietnamese: Hồi nhỏ tôi hay bơi ở con sông gần nhà ông bà.

scenarios.why: Becoming familiar with something new → get used to + V-ing.
scenarios.english: I'm still getting used to driving on the left.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tôi vẫn đang tập quen với việc lái xe bên trái.

scenarios.why: Already familiar → be used to + V-ing.
scenarios.english: Don't worry, I'm used to working under pressure.
scenarios.vietnamese: Đừng lo, tôi quen làm việc dưới áp lực rồi.

scenarios.context: 💬 Catching up with an old friend
scenarios.why: Questions about past habits: Did you use to…?
scenarios.english: Did you use to have long hair in high school?
scenarios.vietnamese: Hồi cấp ba bạn để tóc dài phải không?

quickChecks.question: When I was a child, I ___ afraid of the dark.
quickChecks.explanation: A past state that is no longer true → used to + base verb.

quickChecks.question: She has lived in Hanoi for years, so she ___ the noise.
quickChecks.explanation: Familiar with something now → be used to + noun.

quickChecks.question: It took me a while to get used to ___ up at 5 a.m.
quickChecks.explanation: In 'get used to', 'to' is a preposition → V-ing.

quickChecks.question: ___ you use to live near here?
quickChecks.explanation: Questions: Did + subject + use to (no -d).

sections.heading: Used to + base verb — past habits and states
sections.body: Use used to for things that happened regularly or were true in the past but are not true now. It only exists in the past.
bullets: Positive: used to + base verb
Negative: didn't use to + base verb
Question: Did + subject + use to + base verb?
For present habits, use 'usually' + present simple, NOT 'use to'

examples.english: We used to go to the beach every summer.
examples.vietnamese: Hồi trước mùa hè nào chúng tôi cũng đi biển.

examples.english: He didn't use to like vegetables.

sections.heading: Be used to + V-ing / noun — already familiar
sections.body: Be used to means something is normal for you; it no longer feels strange or difficult. 'To' is a preposition here, so a noun or V-ing follows.

examples.english: I'm used to the heat in Saigon.
examples.vietnamese: Tôi đã quen với cái nóng ở Sài Gòn.

examples.english: She isn't used to speaking in public.
examples.vietnamese: Cô ấy chưa quen nói trước đám đông.

sections.heading: Get used to — the process of becoming familiar
sections.body: Get used to describes the change from strange to normal. Unlike 'used to + verb', it can be used in any tense.

examples.english: You'll get used to the new software quickly.
examples.vietnamese: Bạn sẽ nhanh quen với phần mềm mới thôi.

examples.english: I'm getting used to cooking for myself.

vietnameseTips: Mẹo dịch: 'used to + V' = 'trước đây thường/hay…' (giờ không còn nữa). 'be used to + V-ing' = 'đã quen với…'. 'get used to' = 'dần quen với…'.
Không có 'use to' ở thì hiện tại. Muốn nói 'Tôi thường dậy sớm', hãy dùng 'I usually get up early', không phải 'I use to get up early'.
Trong câu phủ định và câu hỏi với 'did', bỏ -d: 'didn't use to', 'Did you use to…?'.

commonMistakes.wrong: I use to play games every night.
commonMistakes.right: I usually play games every night. / I used to play games every night.
commonMistakes.explanation: 'Use to' không dùng cho thói quen hiện tại. Hiện tại → usually; quá khứ → used to.

commonMistakes.wrong: I'm used to wake up early.
commonMistakes.right: I'm used to waking up early.
commonMistakes.explanation: Sau 'be used to' là V-ing hoặc danh từ.

commonMistakes.wrong: Did you used to live here?
commonMistakes.right: Did you use to live here?
commonMistakes.explanation: Sau 'did', động từ trở về nguyên thể → 'use to'.

practice.vietnamese: Trước đây tôi hay đi làm bằng xe buýt.
practice.english: I used to go to work by bus.

practice.vietnamese: Tôi chưa quen ăn đồ cay.
practice.english: I'm not used to eating spicy food.

practice.vietnamese: Bạn sẽ dần quen với thời tiết ở đây.
practice.english: You'll get used to the weather here.

lessons.title: Reported Speech
lessons.description: Tell someone what another person said — shift tenses, pronouns, and time words correctly, and report questions without question word order.
lessons.rule: After a past reporting verb (said, told, asked), move the tense one step back and change pronouns and time/place words to fit the new situation.
examples: "I'm tired." → She said (that) she was tired.
"We will call you." → They said they would call me.
"Where do you live?" → He asked me where I lived.
"Don't be late." → My boss told me not to be late.

tldr.rule: Reporting in the past? Step the tense back: am → was, will → would, did → had done.
tldr.example: "I can help you." → He said he could help me.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: "Tôi giúp bạn được." → Anh ấy nói là anh ấy có thể giúp tôi.

scenarios.context: 💼 Passing on a message at work
scenarios.why: Reporting instructions → tell + person + (not) to + V.
scenarios.english: The manager told us to finish the report by Friday.
scenarios.vietnamese: Quản lý bảo chúng tôi hoàn thành báo cáo trước thứ Sáu.

scenarios.why: A statement reported later → backshift the tense.
scenarios.english: Your mum called. She said she was coming over tonight.
scenarios.vietnamese: Mẹ bạn gọi đấy. Bác nói tối nay bác sẽ qua.

scenarios.why: Advice → advise / tell someone to do something.
scenarios.english: The doctor advised me to drink more water.
scenarios.vietnamese: Bác sĩ khuyên tôi uống nhiều nước hơn.

scenarios.why: Reported questions use statement word order.
scenarios.english: They asked me why I wanted to leave my last job.
scenarios.vietnamese: Họ hỏi tôi vì sao tôi muốn nghỉ công việc trước.

quickChecks.question: "I am working from home." → She said she ___ from home.
quickChecks.explanation: Present continuous steps back to past continuous.

quickChecks.question: "Have you finished?" → He asked me if I ___.
quickChecks.explanation: Present perfect steps back to past perfect.

quickChecks.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: She asked me where did I work.
She asked me where I worked.
She asked me where do I work.
She asked me where I worked?
quickChecks.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order and no question mark.

quickChecks.question: "Don't touch the screen." → The guide told us ___ the screen.
quickChecks.explanation: Negative command → tell someone + not to + base verb.

sections.heading: Backshift — one step back in time
sections.body: When the reporting verb is in the past (said, told, explained), the original tense usually moves one step back.
bullets: present simple → past simple: "I like it." → she said she liked it
present continuous → past continuous
present perfect / past simple → past perfect
will → would, can → could, may → might, must → had to (or must)

examples.english: "I've lost my passport." → He said he had lost his passport.
examples.vietnamese: Anh ấy nói là anh ấy đã làm mất hộ chiếu.

examples.english: "I can't come." → She said she couldn't come.
examples.vietnamese: Cô ấy nói là cô ấy không đến được.

sections.heading: Pronouns, time and place words
sections.body: Change any words that depend on who is speaking, and when and where.
bullets: I / we → he / she / they; my → his / her
now → then; today → that day; tomorrow → the next day / the following day
yesterday → the day before / the previous day; here → there; this → that

examples.english: "I'll see you tomorrow." → She said she would see me the next day.
examples.note: If you report it on the same day, 'tomorrow' can stay.

sections.heading: Reporting questions and commands
sections.body: Reported questions use statement word order (subject before verb) and no question mark. Use if/whether for yes/no questions. Commands and requests use tell/ask + person + (not) to + base verb.

examples.english: "Are you free?" → He asked if I was free.
examples.vietnamese: Anh ấy hỏi tôi có rảnh không.

examples.english: "What time does the train leave?" → I asked what time the train left.
"Please sit down." → She asked us to sit down.

sections.heading: When you don't need to backshift
sections.body: If the information is still true, or the reporting verb is in the present, you can keep the original tense.

examples.english: He said (that) the earth goes around the sun.
examples.note: A general truth — no backshift needed.

examples.english: Lan says she is running late.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt chỉ cần thêm 'nói là…', 'bảo là…' mà không đổi động từ. Tiếng Anh thì phải lùi thì: 'Cô ấy nói cô ấy mệt' → 'She said she was tired'.
'Say' không đi thẳng với người nghe: nói 'She said (to me) that…' hoặc 'She told me that…', không nói 'She said me…'.
Câu hỏi gián tiếp không đảo ngữ: 'He asked where I lived', không phải 'He asked where did I live'. Mẹo: sau 'asked' cứ viết như câu kể bình thường.

commonMistakes.wrong: She said me that she was busy.
commonMistakes.right: She told me that she was busy.
commonMistakes.explanation: 'Tell' + người nghe; 'say' không có tân ngữ chỉ người đi liền sau.

commonMistakes.wrong: He asked me what was my name.
commonMistakes.right: He asked me what my name was.
commonMistakes.explanation: Câu hỏi gián tiếp dùng trật tự câu kể: chủ ngữ đứng trước động từ.

commonMistakes.wrong: My mother told me don't go out late.
commonMistakes.right: My mother told me not to go out late.
commonMistakes.explanation: Mệnh lệnh phủ định gián tiếp → told + người + not to + V.

practice.vietnamese: Anh ấy nói rằng anh ấy sẽ đến muộn.
practice.english: He said (that) he would be late.

practice.vietnamese: Cô ấy hỏi tôi đã từng đến Đà Lạt chưa.
practice.english: She asked me if I had ever been to Da Lat.

practice.vietnamese: Giáo viên bảo chúng tôi đừng dùng điện thoại trong lớp.
practice.english: The teacher told us not to use our phones in class.

lessons.title: Linking Words: Contrast, Cause & Result
lessons.description: Although, despite, however, because of, therefore — each needs a different grammar pattern. Get them right and your writing instantly sounds more mature.
lessons.rule: Conjunctions (although, because, so) join two clauses. Prepositions (despite, because of) take a noun or V-ing. Adverbs (however, therefore) start a new sentence and take a comma.
examples: Although it was raining, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out.
It was raining. However, we went out.
The flight was delayed because of the storm, so we missed the meeting.

tldr.rule: Although/because + clause. Despite/because of + noun. However/therefore + comma, new sentence.
tldr.example: Despite being tired, she finished the report. Therefore, the team met the deadline.
tldr.exampleVietnamese: Dù mệt, cô ấy vẫn hoàn thành báo cáo. Vì vậy, cả nhóm kịp hạn chót.

scenarios.why: Clear signposting earns marks for coherence and cohesion.
scenarios.english: However, this view ignores the cost to taxpayers.
scenarios.vietnamese: Tuy nhiên, quan điểm này bỏ qua chi phí mà người đóng thuế phải gánh.

scenarios.context: 📧 Explaining a delay to a customer
scenarios.why: Cause → result with 'due to' and 'as a result'.
scenarios.english: Due to a system error, your order was delayed. As a result, we have refunded the shipping fee.
scenarios.vietnamese: Do lỗi hệ thống, đơn hàng của quý khách bị chậm. Vì vậy, chúng tôi đã hoàn lại phí vận chuyển.

scenarios.why: Conceding a point with 'although' shows nuance.
scenarios.english: Although remote work is convenient, it can feel lonely.
scenarios.vietnamese: Mặc dù làm việc từ xa tiện lợi, nó có thể khiến người ta thấy cô đơn.

scenarios.why: Formal result linkers sound professional.
scenarios.english: Sales rose by 20%; therefore, we plan to hire two more staff.
scenarios.vietnamese: Doanh số tăng 20%; do đó, chúng tôi dự định tuyển thêm hai nhân viên.

quickChecks.question: ___ the traffic, I arrived on time.
quickChecks.explanation: 'The traffic' is a noun phrase → 'despite' ('although' needs a clause).

quickChecks.question: He studied hard. ___, he failed the test.
quickChecks.explanation: A new sentence showing contrast → 'However,' with a comma.

quickChecks.question: The match was cancelled ___ heavy rain.
quickChecks.explanation: 'Heavy rain' is a noun phrase → 'because of'.

quickChecks.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Although she was ill, but she came.
Although she was ill, she came.
Despite she was ill, she came.
She was ill, however she came.
quickChecks.explanation: Never use 'although' and 'but' together — one linker per contrast.

sections.heading: Three grammar types of linkers
sections.body: Linkers with the same meaning can follow different grammar patterns. Learn the pattern, not just the meaning.
bullets: Conjunction + clause: although, even though, while, because, since, as, so
Preposition + noun / V-ing: despite, in spite of, because of, due to, owing to
Sentence adverb + comma: however, nevertheless, therefore, as a result, consequently

examples.english: Even though he's rich, he lives simply.
examples.vietnamese: Dù giàu có, anh ấy sống rất giản dị.

examples.english: In spite of having little money, they live happily.

sections.heading: Contrast: although vs despite vs however
sections.body: All three show contrast, but each fits a different structure.
bullets: To use a full clause after despite, add 'the fact that': Despite the fact that it was expensive, …

examples.english: Although the hotel was expensive, the service was poor.
Despite the high price, the service was poor.
The hotel was expensive. However, the service was poor.
examples.note: However starts a new sentence (or follows a semicolon) and takes a comma.

sections.heading: Cause and result
sections.body: Cause linkers explain why something happened; result linkers explain what happened next.
bullets: Cause + clause: because, since, as
Cause + noun: because of, due to, owing to
Result + clause: so (usually after a comma)
Result + new sentence: therefore, as a result, consequently

examples.english: As it was late, we took a taxi.
examples.vietnamese: Vì đã muộn nên chúng tôi đi taxi.

examples.english: Prices have risen sharply. As a result, many families are spending less.
examples.vietnamese: Giá cả tăng mạnh. Kết quả là nhiều gia đình chi tiêu ít hơn.

vietnameseTips: Tiếng Việt quen dùng cặp 'tuy… nhưng…', 'vì… nên…'. Tiếng Anh chỉ dùng MỘT từ nối: 'Although it rained, we went out' hoặc 'It rained, but we went out' — không dùng cả 'although' lẫn 'but', cũng không dùng 'because… so…'.
'Despite' và 'because of' đi với danh từ hoặc V-ing, không đi với mệnh đề. Muốn dùng mệnh đề thì đổi sang 'although' / 'because', hoặc thêm 'the fact that'.
'However' không nối hai mệnh đề bằng dấu phẩy như 'but'. Hãy viết: 'It was cheap. However, it broke quickly.' hoặc dùng dấu chấm phẩy: 'It was cheap; however, it broke quickly.'

commonMistakes.wrong: Because it was raining, so we stayed home.
commonMistakes.right: Because it was raining, we stayed home. / It was raining, so we stayed home.
commonMistakes.explanation: Không dùng 'because' và 'so' trong cùng một câu.

commonMistakes.wrong: Despite it was expensive, I bought it.
commonMistakes.right: Despite the high price, I bought it. / Although it was expensive, I bought it.
commonMistakes.explanation: 'Despite' + danh từ/V-ing; nếu là mệnh đề thì dùng 'although'.

commonMistakes.wrong: The app is useful, however it is slow.
commonMistakes.right: The app is useful. However, it is slow.
commonMistakes.explanation: 'However' bắt đầu câu mới hoặc đứng sau dấu chấm phẩy, và cần dấu phẩy phía sau.

practice.vietnamese: Mặc dù rất mệt, anh ấy vẫn đi tập thể dục.
practice.english: Although he was very tired, he still went to the gym.

practice.vietnamese: Chuyến bay bị hủy vì thời tiết xấu.
practice.english: The flight was cancelled because of bad weather.

practice.vietnamese: Giá thuê nhà tăng. Do đó, nhiều sinh viên phải ở ghép.
practice.english: Rent has increased. Therefore, many students have to share rooms.
